summary.intent: Build an AI product for the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge (Soony game launch): analyze the supplier/ERP data, find where the launch plan contradicts documents, and build agents that detect changes, act (email suppliers, alert buyers) and show evidence.
summary.outcome: Analyzed the data and found the Collector's Edition at risk (overbooked art book receipt, failed statue lot, game card offload, sleeve revision conflict). Then built the alert/voice/push agent (PR #5 into main, 169 tests passing), local OCR evidence anchoring with highlighted sources, a redesigned evidence panel, and a Teams webhook notifier (committed). Briefing pages and interview docs were also created.

repo: The portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Changes must be found by polling and comparing SHA-256, and existing files get replaced under the same name.
Sensitive data lives in the gitignored data/ folder and .env. Only .env.example with an empty token is committed.
Teammates added CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md as a team workflow. Tasks are claimed in PROGRESS.md.

State is in JSON files under ASK_STATE_DIR (Akshat's actions.json is a list, plus decision_status.json) and SQLite for watcher versions. Two modules writing different formats to actions.json caused a conflict.
GitHub showing 'ready to merge' only means no textual conflicts. PR #3 targeted an obsolete branch and was overtaken by a hand merge into akshat/integration.

Akshat's verifier builds the order/confirmation/shipment/receipt/scan graph in code (verifier.linker.build). The card builder in dispatch/decisions flattens evidence into plain strings, which loses file and page.
Tests loaded the real .env and caused 401s in other tests. Fixed by isolating tests from the real .env and moving a shared fixture to conftest.py.
Tesseract with English and Polish is enough for scans, since numbers and IDs are Latin characters. Dockerfile got the tesseract packages.
Teams integration uses a Workflows webhook posting an Adaptive Card whose buttons deep-link to /d/<id> in the app. Configured via ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK and ASK_TEAMS in .env.

code.finding: Anchoring index: PDF word boxes, OCR for scans, table rows. Matches normalized numbers and IDs from evidence text. 320 files indexed in about 36 s, then cached.
Teams Adaptive Card notifier. Posts to a webhook, runs from a background loop, and sends a follow-up when a supplier replies. Adaptive Cards only accept fixed colour names.
Shared send path so the Approve button and a spoken voice 'yes' send supplier emails identically. Only recipients found in portal supplier profiles are actually sent.

workflow: Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change, so a no-file session shows no checkpoint even though hooks fired.
A second Claude session in the same checkout committed and left uncommitted changes on the working branch. Separate worktrees avoid this.
Before editing a teammate's area (DecisionCard.tsx, dispatch/decisions), give a heads-up and check for new commits on their branch. Akshat's parallel push caused a merge conflict.
Delegating bulk cross-checks (200 order confirmations and 59 scans) to a subagent was effective.
Headless Chrome screenshots let the UI be checked before showing it to the user.
Rendering scanned PDFs to images was needed to read them. Some PDFs had empty text.

friction: The portal token was empty at the start, which blocked data access until the user filled it in.
Image uploads from the user did not arrive (empty file icon), so a screenshot of the problem could not be seen.
A merge conflict appeared because Akshat pushed to DecisionCard.tsx in parallel. His new test also failed on real-data machines because cards_file() ignored ASK_DATA_DIR.
A stray uncommitted basic_auth.py change from another session had to be resolved.
The first push of PR #5 was rejected by GitHub with a bare 'failed' and worked on retry.
One alert test was flaky in the full suite and passed in isolation; this was not pursued.
The anchor ranking is heuristic, and common numbers can surface a less fitting source first. Existing verifier cards cite few documents.
The user found the evidence panel unclear about what point it makes, which led to a redesign.
open_items: Push the four anchoring and evidence-panel commits, and the Teams commit, to PR #5. The assistant asked and the user has not yet confirmed. Akshat still needs to merge PR #5 into main.
Create the Teams Workflows webhook and put the URL into .env as ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK. Teams is untested against a real tenant, and the data is confidential.
The PDF example card is handmade from real values in data/state/. A generic check that turns supplier PDFs into cards against SAP still needs a decision on whether it belongs in the verifier.
Send the Karton Nowak offer (8,000 art books, valid 24 h) and answer Boise. This needs a registered sender address and a team inbox.
Update the briefing page, which still shows the 14:00 state, with the 14:37 drop.
Get a euro figure for a missing Collector's copy from Maren for the pitch.
Ask the Lio engineers whether portal data is identical for all teams and whether supplier replies create files.
Decide on cleaning up old sample data and the contract doc, and on the earlier Claude doc.
Demo script, deck and video before the 12:00 hand-in.
